title: Python exception inside a code block
notes: Fixed. `call_python` renders its own diagnostic and raises a module-private `_CodeBlockRaised`, re-raised on the block's `code` key so the line is 2 rather than 0 and the `Python Code error:` category label is gone. The traceback is replaced by the frames whose *code object* came out of this block's `compile` -- the block's own code, including functions it defined -- printed with the source line the interpreter is holding (`linecache` cannot resolve `<code-block>`, which is why the old output showed no source) and a caret from CPython's position table. The test is code-object identity, not the filename this first shipped with: every block compiles under the shared name `<code-block>`, so a filename filter let a function defined in one block and called from another (the `PDL_SESSION` idiom, used by `examples/rag/tfidf_rag.pdl`) put the *other* block's line numbers into this block's source, printing an innocent line of the wrong block under a caret. Frames from another block are named in a `note:` instead. The gutter's numbering caveat is a `note:` too, emitted last among the notes and only when a gutter was printed: the rule paragraph states the rule, and a side-fact about how to read the evidence takes the same shape here as `print(...) writes to stdout` does in E-CODE-002, which is what makes the two siblings look like one tool. Making the filename unique per execution would fix that too, and was rejected: the name is readable from a succeeding program via `traceback.format_exc()`, so it is success-path output and must not move. The excerpt is lstripped and rebased like CPython's own traceback, windowed to 66 characters around the caret, and the builder is total -- an exception whose `__str__` raises degrades the message rather than replacing it with PDL's own error at `:0`. Fix scores 0 deliberately: there is nothing true and useful to say to someone who divided by zero, and the rubric ranks a vacuous `help:` below none; the NameError and ModuleNotFoundError branches of the same diagnostic do carry a checked suggestion and want corpus entries of their own. **Location still scores 1 after phase-3 item 7**, which added `  in code` to this golden: a block path does not lift an entry whose *line* is coarse, and `prog.pdl:2` is still the enclosing `code:` key while the offending statement is on file line 3. The path is coarse in the same way and for the same reason -- `code` is that same enclosing key. Rendering the column (foundation work left undone on purpose, see `get_loc_string`) would not help either; what this entry needs is the file line of the statement, which means mapping `code:N` gutter rows back onto file lines.
